test.title: Why songs stay in the memory

paragraphs.text: Most people can recall the words of a song they have not heard for years, even when they struggle to remember what they did last week. Psychologists at the University of Lindmark set out to discover why musical memories seem so durable.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: In one experiment, volunteers learned short poems, some spoken and some sung to simple tunes. A week later, the sung poems were remembered almost twice as well. The researchers believe that melody gives the brain a second route to the words: if one route fails, the other may still work.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: A second study looked at people with memory loss caused by illness. Many could not name family members, yet they sang along to songs from their youth. Such cases suggest that musical memory is stored in parts of the brain that are damaged later than others.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: The team also found a disadvantage. Songs learned by heart can become stuck, repeating in the mind for hours. This was most common among people who were tired or stressed, and least common among those concentrating on a demanding task.
paragraphs.label: D
